title: Snakebite First-Aid Guide
emergencyMessage: Suspected snakebite? Seek emergency medical care immediately. Do not wait for symptoms.

steps.title: Move Away Safely
steps.description: Move away from the snake to avoid another bite. Do not attempt to catch or handle it.

steps.title: Get Emergency Help
steps.description: Arrange urgent transport to the nearest hospital. Do not delay for snake identification or home treatment.

steps.title: Keep the Person Still
steps.description: Reassure the person and minimise movement. Avoid walking if possible. Arrange transport instead.

steps.title: Remove Tight Items
steps.description: Remove rings, watches, bracelets and tight clothing near the bite before swelling develops.

steps.title: Keep the Limb Still
steps.description: Support the bitten limb and keep it still without tight compression. Do not apply a tourniquet.

steps.title: Monitor and Inform
steps.description: Watch the person's breathing and responsiveness. Tell hospital staff the time and place of the bite if known.

donts.title: Do Not Use a Tourniquet
donts.description: Do not tie a rope, cloth or tight bandage around the bitten limb.

donts.title: Do Not Cut or Suck
donts.description: Do not cut the bite or attempt to suck out venom.

donts.title: Do Not Apply Ice
donts.description: Do not apply ice, heat, chemicals or herbal pastes.

donts.title: Do Not Catch the Snake
donts.description: Never attempt to capture, kill or handle the snake.

donts.title: Do Not Delay Treatment
donts.description: Do not wait for symptoms, traditional remedies or online identification.

disclaimer: Educational information only. This guide does not replace emergency medical care or professional advice.
